subject: Dedicated GPU selection guidance for HelixAI - telemetry-driven sizing
messages:
From: Amalie Petersen <amalie@helixai.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@helixai.com>
Date: 2028-06-20T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated GPU guidance request for HelixAI

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this on. We ran a short cluster telemetry export (attached) and want a short, pragmatic recommendation for Dedicated: which GPU mix (H100 / A100 / L4) gives us the best tradeoff given our workload. High-level constraints:

- Models: two families — 70B dense decoder (high memory/KV pressure) and 13B chat-style decoder (throughput-sensitive).
- Target p95 token latency: <= 150ms for 13B conversational traffic; 70B can tolerate higher latency (up to ~400ms).
- Expected steady QPS: 3k inference requests/min for 13B, 500 req/min for 70B.
- Peak burst factor: ~3x for marketing demos.
- Cost sensitivity: want to keep unit token cost below our current baseline by 20% if possible.

Attachments: helix_telemetry_202806.zip (sample traces + p95 distribution), model_profiles_sample.json (profile of tokenization and KV sizes)

Could you propose an initial Dedicated pool mix, suggested reserved vs burst slots, and any quick ops caveats (cache priming, pre-warm steps)? We need something we can try in a pilot next month.

Thanks,
Amalie
Amalie Petersen
Head of ML Infrastructure, HelixAI

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amalie Petersen <amalie@helixai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-20T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU guidance request for HelixAI

Hi Amalie — thanks for the telemetry export, that helps a lot. Quick read and a few clarifying Qs before we draft numbers: 

1) The 70B prof shows sustained KV working set ~90GB per model instance at 8k context. Is that peak or an aggregate across concurrent requests?
2) For the 13B family, are you using typical batch sizes of 8-16 or lower (1-4) for conversational responses?
3) Do you want single-model isolation (pin 70B to its own reserved pool) or are you open to multiplexing on a mixed pool with fallback?

High-level thinking (short):
- H100: best perf for 70B when you need single-request low latency and high effective memory bandwidth; expensive per-slot but fewer slots required for memory-heavy models.
- A100: good mid-point for throughput; lower per-slot memory vs H100 depending on config (40GB/80GB variants).
- L4: best TCO for smaller / quantized 13B inference where memory pressure is lower — huge token-per-dollar advantage for batched conversational traffic.

Next steps: Ben and Irene will draft a telemetry-driven sizing workbook with three scenarios (conservative-reserve, mixed-reserve+burst, latency-first). Can you confirm answers to the Qs above by EOD? We’ll include suggested reserved counts, burst pools, and quick ops runbook (cache priming + pre-warm).

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amalie Petersen <amalie@helixai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-20T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU guidance request for HelixAI

Amalie — digging into the telemetry and Karthik's Qs, here is a pragmatic pilot recommendation we can stand up in two weeks. Summary first, details after.

Summary (pilot, 6-8 week):
- Reserved pool: 8 H100 slots (for 70B heavy KV models) + 16 L4 slots (for 13B production traffic).
- Burst pool: elastic A100 pool (up to 12 x A100-80GB) to absorb demo/peak bursts and to act as warm overflow for mid-size quantized 13B jobs.
- Routing policy: latency-first for 13B conversation -> prefer L4 when batchable, fallback to A100 for cold/low-batch; 70B pinned to H100 reserved pool with automatic fallback to A100 in extreme peak (graceful degraded p95).
- Cost rationale: L4s lower tokens-per-dollar on batched 13B; H100 reduces slot count and memory fragmentation for 70B. A100 burst reduces reserved commitment while providing memory headroom for mid-range use.

Sizing notes (telemetry-driven assumptions):
- 13B conversational mean tokens per request: 80; typical effective batch 6 — maps to ~2.2k tokens/sec per L4 slot under our runtime. 16 L4 reserved slots => ~211k tokens/min steady (covers base 3k req/min with margin).
- 70B KV working set ~90GB -> H100-80GB variants with fragmenting quantization recommended; each H100 slot can host one active 70B instance with KV caching strategies. 8 H100 reserved slots -> supports 500 req/min profile with queueing headroom; A100 overflow provides extra concurrency during bursts.
- Burst sizing: assume 3x burst; A100 pool sized to absorb additional 24 concurrent slot-equivalents for 20-30 minute bursts.

Ops caveats / runbook highlights:
- Cache priming: pre-warm top 100 prompt prefixes before demo windows to avoid cold-KV penalties.
- Quantization: iterate 8-bit quant for 13B first; evaluate 4-bit for 70B only if quality is validated.
- Autoscale policy: target 60-70% slot utilization on reserved pools; allow 10-15% headroom for GC and pre-warm.
- Monitoring: enable per-model KV cache hit metrics and per-slot tail-latency (p95/p99) alerts.

Attachments included: redwood_accel_mix_v1.xlsx (detailed workbook with tokens-per-second assumptions, cost delta scenarios), short checklist for procurement (DocuSign link prepared).

If this looks good, we’ll produce a formal proposal with line-item reserved counts and pricing offsets for your procurement team.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Dedicated Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. Quick notes and next steps: 

- Confirming the KV working set is per-instance peak; we profiled with 8k context and that matches your note.
- For 13B, batch sizes average 5 during steady-state; good to assume batchable production.
- Procurement would like a line-item quote and the DocuSign ready so we can start the reserved commitment trial.

We’ve reviewed the workbook and the proposed routing policy looks reasonable. Please go ahead and produce the formal quote and I’ll loop in Legal for a quick playbook review. We’ll aim to start the pilot on July 10.
